- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.4) and forecast is significantly above recent mean, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) and forecast is below recent mean, increase forecast by 5–10% to avoid underreaction.  
- If forecast peaks sharply after a spike in sentiment, reduce peak by 10–15% to account for mean reversion.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >15% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast toward that average.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.3 → -0.2 → +0.3), reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% to avoid overfitting.  
- When sentiment is flat (±0.1) and forecast is drifting away from recent 7-day average, apply a “mean reversion” correction: pull forecast toward 7-day average by 5–10%.
